market_question: Will West Ham be relegated from the English Premier League after the 2025–26 season?
reasoning: West Ham are an established mid-table Premier League club with robust finances and an experienced squad; a 34.5% implied relegation chance is wildly above historical benchmarks for similar clubs. Even allowing for managerial changes and unpredictable injuries, a realistic relegation risk sits around 10% – far lower than the market price suggests.
evidence_points: West Ham have finished between 9th and 16th in eight of the last ten Premier League seasons, with only one genuine relegation scare (2022–23) and no drop since 2010–11.
The club’s wage bill and transfer spending consistently rank in the top half of the league, providing a buffer against sudden collapses typical of relegated sides.

Managerial stability and quality depth (including European experience) reduce the tail risk that smaller clubs face – relegation betting markets historically offer odds of ~10–20% for comparable teams.
sources_consulted: Bookmaker odds for relegation one year out (implied probabilities for mid-table teams)
